title: OpenPlan OCR extraction contract (openplan-ocr-extraction.v1)
description: Service-level contract between a planning application (e.g. OpenPlan) and an OCR worker (workers/ocr_worker, or any worker that speaks this contract). The consumer POSTs an OcrRequest to the worker's /api/v1/ocr-requests endpoint with one signed, time-limited link to a PDF; the worker recognises text and POSTs OcrCallback payloads to the consumer's callbackUrl as the job advances. Both directions authenticate with a pre-shared bearer token. THE PAGE IS THE ANCHOR AND THE CONTRACT'S WHOLE POINT: a succeeded callback carries text PER PAGE, one entry per page of the source document in ascending order with no gaps, so an excerpt the consumer later shows a planner can name the page it came from. A page the recogniser found no text on is delivered with an EMPTY string, never omitted — dropping it would silently renumber every page after it. OCR is TRANSCRIPTION: the worker never summarises, never reorders, never repairs, and never reports a certainty, likelihood or confidence for what it read. This file is committed at the repository root and is the single source of truth; the worker's Python constants and the consumer's zod schemas are hand mirrors, each cross-checked against this file by their own test suites. Bump schemaVersion for any breaking change.

requestId.description: Caller-generated idempotency key echoed by every callback. A retried submission with the same requestId must not create a second job; the worker answers the SAME accepted callback body instead.

callbackUrl.description: HTTP(S) endpoint on the consumer that receives OcrCallback payloads. Bearer-authenticated with the shared callback token.

languages.description: Tesseract language codes to recognise with, in priority order (e.g. ["eng"], ["spa","eng"]). REQUIRED TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE CONSUMER RATHER THAN DEFAULTED IN THE WORKER when the deployment cares: OpenPlan is not a United-States-only product, and a worker that silently assumes English would return garbage for a plan adopted in Spanish and give no sign it had done so. The worker refuses a language it has no trained data for, naming the code and what it does have.

maxPages.description: Optional ceiling. A document with more pages than this is REFUSED (a failed callback naming both numbers) rather than truncated — a half-read document whose later pages simply do not exist would be indistinguishable, downstream, from a document that ends there.

maxCallbackBytes.description: Optional ceiling on the serialized size of the succeeded callback, as the CONSUMER will enforce it. The worker measures its assembled payload against this before sending; over the ceiling it sends a failed callback naming the measured size and the ceiling, so the operator meets a sentence instead of a stalled job or a 413 retry loop.

url.description: Signed, time-limited link to the PDF. Must stay valid long enough for the worker to download it; recognition itself happens after the download, so the link does not need to outlive the job.

checksumSha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the source bytes. When present the worker verifies it and FAILS the job naming the mismatch — a corrupted download would otherwise produce recognised text attributed to a document nobody could distrust.

callbackId.description: Unique per delivery. The contract allows redeliveries; consumers dedupe on this.

message.description: One honest sentence naming the stage and the cause. Never a certainty, confidence or likelihood about what was recognised — that would be the machine grading its own transcription.

pageCount.description: Pages in the SOURCE document. On a succeeded callback this must equal pages.length; the worker cross-checks it against the PDF's own page count before sending and fails the job on a mismatch rather than delivering pages whose numbers might have shifted.

pages.description: REQUIRED when status is 'succeeded'. One entry per page of the source, page numbers 1..pageCount ascending with no gaps and no duplicates. A page with no recognised text carries an empty string; it is never omitted, because omitting it would renumber every page after it.

then.description: A succeeded OCR job with no pages is not a success — it is a failure that did not say so.

page.description: 1-based page number in the SOURCE document.

text.description: The recognised text of exactly this page, verbatim in reading order as the recogniser produced it. Empty when nothing was recognised.

languages.description: The languages actually used, which the consumer records: text recognised with the wrong language pack is the failure mode a reader cannot see.

pagesWithText.description: How many of the delivered pages carry any text at all. A COUNT, not a score: it lets the consumer say '148 of 212 pages produced text' instead of implying a quality judgement nobody measured.
